matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When relocating a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal). Rotating a stick changes its type and can create invalid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you move a stick from one character to another or within a character.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick and using it as a diagonal in another character.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For every proposed transformation; ensure the total stick count stays the same.
matchstick.example: Adding a new stick to a character without removing it from any other character.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick relocation, before accepting the new equation.
matchstick.example: Resulting in a V with an extra vertical stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and check that the equality holds after the stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate corrected equation.
matchstick.example: Proposing 'VI = V + I' without checking that the arithmetic holds after the move.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonals (or be transformed by repositioning, not by removal).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to an X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an X, leaving a single diagonal line.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved to a different position inside the same numeral, altering its shape while keeping the character a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change the shape of a numeral (e.g., turn V into X) without involving another character.
matchstick.example: Changing a V into an X by moving one of its diagonal sticks to cross the other diagonal.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved from one character to a different character, altering both; ensure that after the move each character remains a valid numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the solution requires borrowing a stick from one symbol to augment another.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to another I, causing the source I to disappear and the target I to become II.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>', with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.example: Ending the response with just 'V = II + III' instead of the required 'Correct version of the equation: V = II + III'.

matchstick.title: Validate single‑stick relocation feasibility
matchstick.principle: After proposing a corrected equation, verify that the change from the original can be achieved by moving exactly one stick; no other sticks may be added, removed, or repositioned.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before accepting a candidate solution; simulate the move to ensure only one stick changes.
matchstick.example: Suggesting to turn 'III' into 'V' by moving two sticks, which requires more than one stick.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave an empty placeholder. Ensure the resulting equation contains no empty symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from an I.
matchstick.example: Moving the only stick from an I and leaving an empty placeholder where the I used to be.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual stick move and forgets to compute the numeric values of the Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert both sides of the proposed equation to Arabic numbers and confirm the equality before finalising the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model omits the required prefix or misplaces whitespace, causing the parser to miss the final line.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: End the response with exactly 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' and collapse any extra whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats moving a stick as deleting it, forgetting to place it on another character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the source and destination of the moved stick; ensure the stick appears on the target character.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape (e.g., V with one diagonal, X with one diagonal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a multi‑stick numeral without checking that the remaining sticks still form a legal Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After removing a stick, verify that the source numeral is still a valid Roman numeral; if not, the move is illegal.

matchstick.description: Proposed equation not reachable by a single stick move (multiple sticks changed)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model imagines a transformation that would require altering more than one stick, overlooking the single‑stick constraint.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Simulate the exact stick relocation and confirm that only one stick changes; reject any solution that needs additional changes.
